facts.text: Danbury is home to the Forts Folle Avoine Historical Park, featuring reconstructed fur trade posts from the early nineteenth century.
The name Folle Avoine comes from a French term meaning wild oats or rice, referring to the local river complex.
Hunter James Jordan harvested a record-setting white-tailed deer near Danbury in 1914 that remains one of the largest in the world.
The Croix Chippewa Indian Band of the Lake Superior Chippewa hosts an annual pow-wow featuring drums and singers from across North America.
Danbury Days is an annual Fourth of July weekend parade that draws over two thousand five hundred people for food and vendors.
The Village Players Community Theatre was established in 1999 to provide performing arts opportunities for northwestern Wisconsin.
